name: Magi of Hermes

characters.name: Alexander of Jerbiton

description.biography:
An athletic man of Mediterranean looks, in cheap clothes made only of animal products.

Combat, in human shape: fist Init 0, Attack +3, Defense +3, Damage 0; bludgeon Init 0, Attack +5, Defense +3, Damage +2. Soak +2.

Equipment: cheap gear he can abandon if he wanders off in animal shape; his clothes are all animal products, so they change with him. Encumbrance 0. No Twilight Scars.

Experience towards the next score: Mu 15, An 9.

These fifteen years: he joins a well-resourced covenant, works on spells and skills for leading grogs, and goes on preparing for an expedition to Ethiopia.

Animal shapes (pp. 10-12, generic beasts, with the errata's changes to their Qualities). Asp: venomous, its bite takes effect if its Attack Advantage exceeds armor Protection; Bat: Size -9, echo-sight; in famine he turns his party to bats, fed on insects, to stretch supplies; Camel: smells water two miles off, two weeks without drinking; Crocodile: Roll Attack, dragging a bitten victim under or tearing flesh for +6; Lion: claws +15 Attack, +10 Damage. His attendants wear quilted wool armor pinned with bone, and carry bone, horn or ivory weapons at -2 Damage (daggers and knives -1) that break on botches. Water in skins does not transform and is lost: he has found no cure.

Design totals: Abilities 655, Arts 395, Spells 395; 20 xp more than an average magus in this period.

New spells:
Recruiting A Tiny Phalanx: R Touch, D Sun, T Group. Makes a human's weight of scorpions, with a Rego requisite so he can order them; a swarm attacking does +10 damage a round, Soaked as usual. He pours them between two Circles of Beast Warding round a camp. The blocks print level 35, its own entry 30 (Base 5, +1 Touch, +2 Sun, +1 Group, +1 requisite).
Scales of the Scorpions: R Voice, D Diam, T Group. Plates friendly animals, transformed grogs included, in chitin for +3 Soak.
Eyes of the Housecats: R Voice, D Sun, T Group. Cat's sight, for normal action in low light; he likes to march at night.
The Guardian of the Tombs: R Per, D Sun, T Ind. Takes cobra shape: feels movement through the ground and has a poisonous bite; poison bitten into something hollow stays after he changes back, and grogs use it on arrows. A serpent-skin wristband is his focus to end it at will. The blocks print "A Guardian of the Tombs".
The Desert Wanderer: R Per, D Sun, T Ind. Arabian camel shape, with the camel's nose for water; a camel-leather belt ends it at will.
The Lurker in the Rushes: R Touch, D Sun, T Ind. Crocodile shape, for him or one he touches; a crocodile-skin scabbard ends it at will. The blocks print level 30, its own entry 40 (Base 20, +1 Touch, +2 Sun, +1 size).
The Shadow on the Sand: R Per, D Sun, T Ind. Vulture shape, with keen sight; a strand of vulture feathers ends it at will.
A Punishment for Brigands: R Voice, D Sun, T Ind. Turns a human into a mouse, which Circle of Beast Warding can then pen.
A Source of Tremendous Pride: R Voice, D Sun, T Group. Turns servants into a pride of straight-maned lions; a tail spur in his pouch can end it. The males are lazy, so the covenant has a small cadre of women fighters.

reputations.name: Noted writer of travel journals (House Jerbiton)

characters.summary:
A Jerbiton of average height, olive-skinned and dark-haired, who gives his life to exploring the North African deserts. As an apprentice he dreamed of the ruins there, and his easy-going master gave him the skills to find trouble without those to escape it, which he mends later. Scrawny when young and wiry with age, leathered by the Egyptian sun, he dresses as the locals do.

He turns himself and his attendants into animals to cross hard country, leads grogs on expeditions, and writes journals his House values. Story seeds: an expedition to Ethiopia or the Kushite ruins and their wind guardians; a rival whose ship was lost, some say after his clothes burned from a Conflagratious Lanyard.

characters.name: Aurulentus of Jerbiton

invented_spells.name: Eyes of the Sage
invented_spells.description: From the stat block in Magi of Hermes.

description.biography:
A tall, handsome man, brown-haired, with a golden glint in his hazel eyes and fine features, always clean shaven, in close-fitting clothes that show off his athletic build.

Oh Brother, Where Art Thou? (0 points, Init -2, Corpus): he senses the direction, rough distance and health of anyone descended by blood from his great-great-grandfather Alexander. No penetration, words or gestures (InCo Base 3, +3 Bloodline, +1 health).

Combat: fist Init -2, Attack 0, Defense -2, Damage 0. Soak +1. Equipment: tasteful clothes and a wedding ring. Encumbrance 0.

Twilight Scars: his touch cures small children's toothache, his beard grows exceptionally strongly, and dogs take him for a cat.

Experience towards the next score: Cr 1, Co 1, Me 2, Vi 6.

These fifteen years: five years in the lab, pressed by Semira's coming age. Artemis' Fertility takes two seasons and two more to reinvent twice; he learns and twice reinvents Bane of the Decrepit Body, reinvents The Maculate Noblewoman three times, spends four seasons on eight Longevity Rituals and four stabilizing: the breakthrough holds, and he makes rituals for himself and Semira that leave them fertile. Then he empowers Zeno's bond and invents Eyes of the Sage. The last ten years are learning.

Familiar, bound at 34: Zeno the Tortoise, about 20 cm long, a drab brown shell with 15 lumps along it. Magic Might 15; Int 0, Per -2, Pre -5, Com -6, Str -1, Sta +5, Dex +2, Qik -5; Size -4; Soak +12. Virtues Enduring Constitution, Long-Winded, Tough, Unaging; Flaws Noncombatant, Poor Eyesight, Reclusive. Abilities Awareness 2, Brawl 2, High German 5, Latin 5, Greek 4, Survival 5. Powers: Retreat of Invulnerability (1 point, Init -5): in his shell he is immune to all non-magical harm; Grant Virtue (Unaging) (5 points, Init -5): one person, for as long as he likes (Guardians of the Forests p. 32). Vis: 2 pawns of Creo in his shell. Bond: Bronze +3, Silver +1, Gold +1 (CrCo Lab Total 40).

Zeno's bond also carries Mental Communication: he and Aurulentus are in constant touch by words, images and feeling (CrMe 15).

The breakthrough is a Minor Hermetic Breakthrough under Houses of Hermes: True Lineages p. 26; six seasons stabilizing in all.

New spells:
Widening the River Styx: Ritual, R Touch, D Mom, T Ind. Settles a minor aging crisis; the target must still rest out the season.
Artemis' Fertility: R Touch, D Moon, T Ind. Raises the target's fertility; it cannot promise conception, and other magi doubt it works.
Pose Clotho's Question: R Touch, D Mom, T Ind. Says if a woman is pregnant; fails on men.
Pose Nona's Question: R Touch, D Mom, T Ind. Pregnancy and the months left; if none, the exact date in her cycle. Fails on men.
The Maculate Noblewoman: R Touch, D Mom, T Ind. Finds the true cause of a target's infertility.
Verifying the Presence of Artemis' Blessing: R Touch, D Sun, T Ind. Tells the caster at once of a conception in the target.
Phantasmal Troupe: R Voice, D Conc, T Ind. Illusory music from a chosen direction, a full troupe if wished; Finesse sets the quality. Invented by his parens Altus.

characters.summary:
A magus from a family of mages: the fifth straight generation of seventh sons, under a prophecy that the seventh son of the seventh generation will reshape magic. The line began when Askanius loved a nymph of Artemis in Greece, and each father has sired seven sons his own way: charm (Alexander, Antipater), passive Corpus magic (Alboin), love magic (Altus). Aurulentus means to father all seven on one woman, his true love Semira, so he devotes his career to health, fertility and children, and makes a Longevity Ritual that leaves its users fertile.

His own seventh son, Arbus Tutus, has two daughters and shows little wish for more, or for women, so the grandson the prophecy needs is in doubt. His spells and devices for mothers and children fill his covenant. Story seeds: magi who want the fertile Longevity Ritual; the covenant's unusual birth rate.
characters.secrets: The prophecy may be nothing: the priest and the nymph could have been faeries wagering they could fool seven generations of magi.

characters.name: Conscientia of Bonisagus

abilities.name: Finesse
abilities.specialty: getting it right the first time

invented_spells.name: Fell the Mighty Trunk
invented_spells.description: From the stat block in Magi of Hermes.

description.biography:
Combat: dodge Init 0, Defense 0; fist Init 0, Attack 0, Defense 0, Damage -1; kick Init -1, Attack 0, Defense -1, Damage +2. Soak -2.

Twilight Scars: lights cast shadows of people not in the room, and her reflection is very slightly translucent.

These fifteen years: settled in her post, she gives much time to her own projects: sixteen seasons inventing spells and items, and one reinventing her longevity ritual.

Familiar: Aureus, an exotic red bird with a golden ruff, the gift of a grateful patron. Magic Might 20 (Ignem); Int +2, Per +1, Pre +1, Com 0, Str -6, Sta 0, Dex +1, Qik +5; Size -3; Soak 0. Cords Gold +2, Silver +0, Bronze +2. Abilities Artes Liberales 1, Athletics 6, Bargain 3, Folk Ken 3, French 5, Latin 4, Magic Theory 3. Loyal +3, Patient +2, Inquisitive +1, Terrified of Blue Potions +1. Reincarnation (15 points): dying with 15 or more Might he burns and rises within an hour with 1 Might. Bond: Speech, Shared Senses.

Exciting Experimentation (Minor, Hermetic): on any experimentation table she rolls two dice instead of one (errata), and the storyguide applies the more amusing result.

Items she has made (the book does not date them). Apollo's Lyre: a brass lyre with a song on each string (CrIm 10, 3/day), a popular Lab Text. Cooking Stone (CrIg 15): boils the water it is dropped in. Cultellus (PeVi 37, Pen +32, 50/day): a kitchen knife that dispels a Parma of 6 or lower; she claims she never finished it and burned her notes. Dico Calculus: a stone for a blind Criamon that sees a page (InIm 18) and puts it in the user's mind (CrMe 26). Ferramenta Glacies (ReAq 14): a pick that freezes water. Hermes' Horn (ReAn 40, 1/day): calms up to 1,000 beasts for the day. Mjolnir's Equal (PeTe(He) 25): a hammer that destroys metal or wood it touches. Shulpea's Bowl (CrHe 28): refills with clean, dull food every two minutes. Traveler's Cloak (MuTe(Ig) 25, 1/day): softens and warms the ground till sunrise. Vessel of Etain's Children: a necklace whose fittings turn blood to polished stone (MuAq(Te) 23), keeping Arcane Connections. Vulcan's Favored (CrTe 29): a seal keeping a tool as new, by her new guideline CrTe 15, repair a crafted item.

Charged items and potions she favors: Pneum Flask (ReAu 5), steals a breath as an Arcane Connection; Elixir of Morning's Afterthought (CrCo 20), cures a hangover; Magic Spice (MuIm 5), makes any food taste a feast; Ink of the Unseen Circle (PeIm 15), hides a ring; Potion of Vulcan's Appeasement (PeIg 20), quenches a house fire; Message in a Bottle (CrMe 5), a message in the drinker's mind; The Wakeful Nightmare (ReMe 20), bars sleep for a Moon, with mounting Fatigue and wounds; Whistle of Warning (ReMe 35), Visions of the Infernal Terrors on a group; Door in a Bottle (PeTe 5); Disenchanting Concoction (PeVi 40, Pen +30), as Winds of Mundane Silence.

New spells:
Doublet of Silk, That's Impenetrable: As Doublet of Impenetrable Silk, but the clothing also really turns to silk.
Pests of a Colossal Size: R Voice, D Sun, T Group. Swells the lice and fleas on the targets to huge, often hostile, size. The blocks print level 35, its own entry 30 (Base 4, +2 Sun, +2 Group, +2 Voice).
Epona's Bane: R Voice, D Mom, T Group. Panics a small unit of horses; riders roll Str + Ride 12+ or are thrown.
Summon the Eldritch Bond: R Voice, D Sun, T Ind. Sends a biting insect to bite a target and come back, its blood an Arcane Connection. With Pests of a Colossal Size it reaches further and loses all subtlety.
Be Rid the Tell Tale Smoke: R Touch, D Ring, T Circle. Destroys all smoke in the circle. Learned from her parens.
Touch of the Blessed Virgin: Ritual, R Touch, D Mom, T Ind. Restores a woman's maidenhood.
Statim Sessio: R Touch, D Sun, T Ind. Creates a comfortable wooden chair.
Evening's Comfort: R Touch, D Sun, T Per. Keeps her bed warm until sunrise.
Palm of Odorous Flame: As Palm of Flame, with a random smell at each casting, most often elderberry.
Veneficus Enigma: R Touch, D Conc, T Ind. An illusory puzzlebox: Int + Artes Liberales against her Int + Artes Liberales + 5 opens it, often to a prize.
Spy the Approaching Grog: R Touch, D Conc, T Room. Peers into the room beyond a wall; made to be cast forcelessly so it cannot scry on a magus.
Circle of Undisturbed Rest: R Touch, D Ring, T Circle. Keeps sights and sounds from leaving a camp, which shows as a silent black patch. Errata: PeIm(Re) 25 (Base 4, +1 Touch, +2 Ring, +1 Rego, +1 changing image), not the book's ReIm 5.
Robed in Angelic Beauty: R Voice, D Conc, T Group. Lends the speaker perfect beauty and a holy aura. A Gifted speaker is taken for a devil in disguise. The +30 block prints CrMe 25, the +45 CrMe 30, its own entry CrMe(Im) 25.
Apollo's Fearful Gaze: R Voice, D Sun, T Ind. Light gives pain: moon or candle -1, torch -3, bonfire -5, daylight Incapacitated. The +30 block and its entry print level 30, the +45 block 20.
Conjure the Ocean's Breath: R Touch, D Moon, T Part. Turns a patch of dirt to salt until the Moon ends; quick trade goods.
Armatura Vitrea: R Voice, D Diam, T Ind. Turns armor to glass: Protection 2, Load 3; a weapon's blow shatters it for an extra simple die of damage.
Saving the Apprentice's Time: R Touch, D Mom, T Room. An hour's dusting done in a moment.
Foras Vim: R Voice, D Mom, T Group. A choking cloud of grit: casting in it needs Sta + Concentration 12+. She has long meant to master it for fast casting.
Carve Domain: R Touch, D Mom, T Part. Destroys a channel of up to 10,000 cubic feet of earth.

characters.summary:
A village girl from near Carcassonne, a prodigy of theory whose simplest spells fizzled. Her Tytalus master raged at her until a Bonisagus saw what she was and took her to Durenmar. She assisted in high experiments, the last of which wrecked the lab and sent her parens into Twilight. Since her Gauntlet she has stayed in that lab, awaiting his return, and later takes a librarian's post in the Great Library.

She makes Lab Texts, casting tablets and items to order, bartering for equipment and supplies. She pads her estimates so she can finish early and seem a miracle worker, or spends the spare time on the spell her parens was developing, whose nature the storyguide decides. Story seeds: the unfinished spell; a patron's item with a side effect.
characters.secrets: Cultellus, the Parma-dispelling knife she says she never finished, is listed among her works; its patron never came back for it.

characters.name: Gwidion of Verditius

description.biography:
Deeply wrinkled now, leaning harder on his stick, the price of starting a longevity ritual so late.

Combat: dodge Init -1, Defense -1; fist Init -1, Attack -1, Defense -1, Damage 0; kick Init -2, Attack -1, Defense -2, Damage +3. Soak +3.

Equipment: peasant work clothes in his pack, a basic survival kit, and handmade portable gardening tools. Encumbrance none.

These fifteen years: his magic builds the farms that earn the covenant most of its income. At 50 he serves as a lab assistant in trade for a longevity ritual: 14 pawns of Creo vis, +5, with the covenant's +1 an aging modifier of 6. 225 xp in Abilities, 75 in Arts, 120 levels of spells.

New spells:
Circle of Eternal Spring: R Touch, D Ring, T Circle. Plants in the circle grow well, as The Bountiful Feast.
Ladder Of Ivy: R Voice, D Sun, T Ind. A sturdy ivy ladder about twenty paces long, gone at sunset or sunrise.
Fast Grow: R Touch, D Sun, T Ind. Brings a plant to full maturity in a day or night, if cast soon after sunrise or sunset.
Gigantic Growth: R Touch, D Sun, T Ind. A plant grows a hundredfold until sunset or sunrise.
Blades of Grass, Leaves of Cutting: R Voice, D Sun, T Group. Grass and leaves turn sword-sharp, barring the way even to the armored.
Prune Plant: Printed Pe(Re)He 20 in its own entry, level 5 in the blocks. R Voice, D Mom, T Ind. Reshapes a plant, as skilled pruning, without adding to it or killing it.
Wilt: R Voice, D Mom, T Part. A plant wilts and dies. The blocks print level 25, its own entry 35.
Prison Floral: R Touch, D Ring, T Circle. Holds aggressively Warped plants inside the circle. The blocks print level 4, its own entry 30.
Ring of Ever Bloom: R Touch, D Ring, T Circle. Plants keep blooming out of season.
Controlled Growth: Ritual, R Touch, D Year, T Ind. Shapes a plant's growth for the year, as a fine gardener would.
Tree Top Walk: R Voice, D Conc, T Group. Branches bend so he can walk from tree to tree. The +15 block prints level 15, all the others and its entry 25.
Warmth of the Wood: R Touch, D Sun, T Part. Warms bark or planks to the touch. The blocks print level 4, its own entry 10.
Frosted Timber: R Touch, D Sun, T Part. Cools bark or planks to the touch.
Tilled Soil: R Voice, D Mom, T Part. Tills 1,000 cubic paces of soil.
Mold the Earth within Sight: R Sight, D Mom, T Part. Shapes earth and stone equal to a hundred men, not metals or gems. Errata: level 25, +1 stone (the blocks agree; its own entry prints 30).

characters.summary:
Gwidion Griffith, a four-foot, curly-haired Welshman, tanned and weathered from a life with his hands in the soil, who looks a peasant but for his rune-cut staff and satchel. Once a rising star of his gild and House, he broke with his master at Tribunal, voted against the gild on vis rights, earned its enmity, and left Durenmar in disgust for the woods and farms of Wales.

Defending villagers from bandits threw him into Twilight and a vision of the World Tree. He settled in a nearly empty wood to study it and has not left. His covenant, a living tree, runs on enchanted plants, with farmland, then honey, for income. Story seeds: an old feud with the Oak Gild; a forest of awakened trees; what happens to it all at his death or Final Twilight.

characters.name: Hugh of Flambeau

invented_spells.name: Blunt the Viper's Fangs
invented_spells.description: From the stat block in Magi of Hermes.

description.biography:
A tall, broad-shouldered man, heavy-browed, squat-featured and broken-nosed, in excellent condition. Short hair, no beard, though he often forgets to shave for days; he could pass for a common soldier. He is growing grizzled, with a few small scars.

Combat: Tonatris Init 0, Attack +6, Defense +6, Damage +4; Troll's Wife Init +1, Attack +18, Defense +12, Damage +13, from horseback Attack +21, Defense +15. Soak 16 in armor with the Bronze Cord, +3 with Gift of the Bear's Fortitude, +3 with Doublet of Impenetrable Silk. No Twilight Scars.

Equipment: Troll's Wife, Tonatris. Encumbrance -1 (Load 9, Burden 3).

Experience towards the next score: Pe 8.

From the Legion of Mithras: Strong-Willed, Dutybound. From his familiar: True Friend. The block prints Puissant Brawl where earlier blocks have Puissant Great Weapon; the +2 stays on Great Weapon, so this is taken as a misprint.

Gird the Warrior (0 points, Init 0, Terram): with a few words and a sweep of his hands his clothes become full metal scale, Protection 7, Load 7, until he dismisses it (MuAn(He,Te) 30, R Touch, D Conc, T Group).

These fifteen years: a familiar, a talisman and an apprentice. One season forging the bond, two empowering it with Ride of the Einherjar, four on Troll's Wife, five training the apprentice; 90 levels of spells, 116 xp in Arts, 154 in Abilities.

Familiar: Bathild, a magical roan charger the colour of dried blood, who claims Sleipnir's descent; Hugh won her from an einheri by starting a war between two villages, deep in the supposed Order of Odin's lands. Bond (ReTe Lab Total 43): Gold +1, Silver +1, Bronze +3. Magic Might 8 (Animal); Int -3, Per +1, Pre 0, Com -4, Str +4, Sta +3, Dex -1, Qik +2; Size +2; Season Summer; Confidence 2 (6). Kick Init +7, Attack +8, Defense +9, Damage +5; Soak +5. Loyal to Hugh +3, Vain +3, Brave +2, Chatty +1. Abilities Athletics 4, Awareness 3, Brawl 4, Concentration 2, Faerie Lore 2, Folk Ken 3, Local Area Lore 3, Magic Lore 3, Order of Hermes Lore 2, Leadership 3, Swim 2, Wilderness Sense 4. Vis: 2 Animal, in her hooves. Power: Beast and Rider As One (4 points, Init -2): the rider's legs meld to her and their minds work together; no Ride rolls, no limit of +3 on his Ride bonus in combat, no falling off or dismounting.

Bond power Ride of the Einherjar (ReAn 27, 3/day): she runs on air until her feet touch ground.

Talisman: Troll's Wife, a long bearded axe of steel and silver on a holly haft banded in brass, carved with horses, eagles and wolves, six discs of amber and bloodstone near the head. Only the haft is enchanted, so Magic Resistance does not stop the blade. Excellent quality (City & Guild pp. 69-70): +3 Attack and Defense; otherwise a pole axe. 12 pawns to open, now full. Attunements: +3 Corpus, +4 blood and wounds, +4 demons and angels, +7 harm or repel faeries.

Its first effect: Fell the Faerie (PeVi 23, Pen 20, 6/day): on the words "ferrum et fraxinus", a haft strike costs a faerie 15 Might.

Tonatris, a Roman caestus of iron-plated leather, opened with 10 pawns, five used. Thumb between ring and little fingers: Night-Time Thunder (ReMe 20, Pen +12, 12/day, D Diam) puts the target to sleep. Thumb between middle and ring fingers: Vaulting Lightning (ReCo 30, Pen +12, 12/day) throws the target 5 paces for +8 damage, doubled by a wall or hard landing.

New spells:
Assume the Stature of the Giants of Eld: R Per, D Diam, T Ind. +3 Size with gear, wounds every 8 points, Characteristics unchanged; An, He and Te casting requisites usually needed for gear.
Avalanche of Flesh and Steel: R Touch, D Conc, T Group. Up to ten men run as fast as a horse, adding their Athletics, up to +3, to the first Attack.
The Blessing of Starkad: R Touch, D Sun, T Part. Two more arms: +3 to climbing and Strength tasks, and a second set of weapons, two attacks a round alone or an extra uncounted member in a group. By a new guideline: MuCo 5, add or take away human parts so the target no longer looks human, T Part.
Turb of Giants: R Touch, D Diam, T Group. As the Stature of the Giants on ten men up to Size +1.
Halt the Piercing Shafts: R Per, D Diam, T Ind. Wood and metal missiles fall at his feet.
Breaking the Captain's Baton: R Voice, D Mom, T Ind. The leader forgets how to coordinate a Trained Group, until he relearns it by practice; the squad fights Untrained unless another takes over.
Blunting the Iron's Bite: R Voice, D Diam, T Ind. A blade's total damage, Attack Advantage included, is halved, rounded up; Magic Resistance can block it, so he often casts it forcelessly.
The Wizard's Parry: Errata: R Voice, D Mom, T Ind, no gestures, without penalty. Deflects one melee blow he is aware of, wholly away from him; his fast-cast defense (Base 2, +2 Voice, +1 no gestures). Herbam requisite for wooden weapons.
Disarm the Warrior: R Voice, D Mom, T Ind. Pulls an object to him with Strength +5, opposed if held; Dex + Athletics 9+ to catch it.
The Instant Ring Fort: R Touch, D Mom, T Part. Throws up a ring of packed earth four paces across, two thick, eight feet high, from a ditch around him.
Circular Wall of Shields: R Touch, D Sun, T Group. Up to twenty shields orbit up to ten people, cover against missiles and, by Per + Finesse plus the shield's Defense, melee. A shield has Soak 3 and breaks at over 10 points in a blow.

characters.summary:
Hugh Hostis was found at fourteen working as a street gang's heavy, frightening people with his Gift, and trained in the School of Ramius, which pairs mundane attacks with magical defense. An excellent soldier, half-deaf from blows to the head, he believes his mother's tale of valkyrie blood and their armor. Always in the front line, he casts defenses on his fellows; grogs respect his skill and fear his temper. His favorite trick is to wound a supernatural foe, then use the blood on his blade as an Arcane Connection.

After nearly fifty years he is a prominent member of his Tribunal, hunting Marched magi with loyal grogs. Story seeds: a Wizard's March that needs a hoplite; his bargain with an einheri; the supposed Order of Odin.
characters.secrets: Two decades out of apprenticeship he was initiated into the Legion of Mithras (The Mysteries Revised pp. 118-122), and holds its second rank, the Bride. Its errands take him beyond the Order's lands after rumored hostile magicians; he has slain several hedge wizards and thinks none was a real threat, but obeys.

characters.name: Julia of Ex Miscellanea

invented_spells.name: Ward Against the Faeries of the Wood
invented_spells.description: From the stat block in Magi of Hermes.

invented_spells.name: Unseen Porter
invented_spells.description: From the stat block in Magi of Hermes.

invented_spells.name: Unraveling the Fabric of Herbam
invented_spells.description: From the stat block in Magi of Hermes.

description.biography:
A plain, dumpy woman, hunched from the loom, her hands forever stained with dye. Wiry black hair sparsely covers her whole body, and her irises are as black as her pupils, which unsettles people. With her trade grown, she dresses well to suit her clients, in fabrics of her own invention and dyes of her own recipes, to show off her wares.

Casting sigil: a thread-like weave. Voting sigil: an embroidered swatch of cloth.

Twilight scars: her arms are permanently dyed blue; loose fibres braid or knot themselves near her; she has a constant musky smell.

Combat: dodge Init 0, Defense 0. Soak +4, with the Bronze Cord. Encumbrance 0.

Last 15 years: invented 90 levels of spells; found and bonded Tetrix and enchanted Snap of Awakening (2 seasons); made her paltry Longevity Ritual (1 season), an embroidered pouch at her neck, -4 to Aging rolls with an extra pawn of vis; opened the Loom and instilled both effects (4 seasons); made and attuned the shears and instilled Sever Wood and Bone (3 seasons). She began training an apprentice who helped with these (2 seasons). 145 xp in Arts and 125 in Abilities. She has 1 xp past her Vim score.

Her Side Effect makes every spell fade slowly instead of ending: hardly noticeable at Momentary or Diameter, about an hour at Sun, a day at Moon or Year. Enduring Magic stretches this too, so a spell that has lasted four Moons takes four days to fade. Rego craft magic is in Covenants page 49, Craft Magic in Houses of Hermes: Societates pages 131-132. Her Faerie Blood turns her own body weight of raw fibre into cloth each day.

Familiar: Tetrix the Blackcock, a male black grouse with black plumage, red wattles, white wing-bars and a lyre-shaped tail, about four feet tall when upright. She chose him for the pun of textrix on tetrix, and found a fierce hunter of spiders. Magic Might 12 (Animal), Summer. Int -3, Per +2, Pre -1, Com -2, Str -3, Sta +3, Dex 0, Qik +2. Size -2. Confidence 1 (3). Virtues and Flaws: Magic Animal; Gossip, Student of Faerie; True Friend (familiar bond); Clumsy, Non-Combatant. Magical Qualities: Greater Power, No Fatigue; Gift of Speech, Improved Abilities (twice), Improved Defense, Improved Soak. Qualities: Camouflage, Ambush Predator, Hardy. Traits: Brave +3, Loyal to Julia +3, Inquisitive +1, Grouse (essential) +3. Beak Init +2, Attack +7, Defense +7, Damage -2; dodge Init +5, Defense +7. Soak +7, with the Bronze Cord. Wounds -1 (1-3), -3 (4-6), -5 (7-9), Incapacitated (10-12), Dead (13+). Abilities: Athletics 3 (flying), Awareness 4 (food), Brawl 4 (dodging), Faerie Lore 3 (faerie animals), Hunt 4 (spiders), Low German 3 (Flemish), Magic Theory 2 (enchantment), Music 2 (grouse-songs), Penetration 2 (Stand Your Ground), Stealth 4 (stalking insects), Survival 5 (moorland). Vis: 3 pawns, in feathers. He gets +3 to Stealth when still, and +3 to Attack in the first round against insects unaware of him.

Tetrix's powers. No Fatigue (0 points, constant): no Fatigue levels, no sleep, no unconsciousness. Stand Your Ground (2 points, Init +4, Corpus or Animal): rearing up freezes a person or animal while he confronts her, or for another point until he leaves her presence (ReCo(An) 20; Base 5, +1 Eye, +1 Conc, +1 requisite; Greater Power gives 30 levels, +4 Init, +10 Penetration).

Familiar bond, Rego Animal Lab Total 38: Gold Cord +2, Silver Cord +1, Bronze Cord +2. Snap of Awakening (ReMe 7, Pen 0, 3/day, Touch, Momentary, Individual): Tetrix wakes her at once, and as he never sleeps he always keeps watch (Base 4, +1 Touch; +2 3/day). Silent Speech (CrMe 15, Pen 0, unlimited, Touch, Momentary, Individual): two effects letting them share words, images and emotions each way (Base 4, +1 Touch; +10 unlimited). He was made by the rules of Realms of Power: Magic, chapter 4.

Talisman, Forfex Princeps: clothier's shears two feet long, of iron inlaid with gold, copper and lead filigree, opened with ten pawns of Vim vis. Attunements: +2 shaping fabric (shears), +7 harm or repel faeries (iron), +4 deftness (copper), +4 wards (lead). Sever Wood and Bone (PeAn(He) 12, Pen 0, 3/day, Touch, Momentary, Individual): cuts any animal or plant stuff the blades close on, mostly bone or wood (Base 4, +1 Touch, +1 requisite; +2 3/day).

Loom of the Kabouters: a beautiful vertical loom all of carved elm, without a metal part, its only other pieces removable stone weights. Named for the small Flemish urban faeries. Opened with ten pawns of Vim vis; six spaces are free. Loom of Elfin Proportions (MuHe 23, Pen 0, 6/day, Personal, Concentration, Individual): shrinks it to a tenth in each dimension, from six feet to seven inches, and she keeps it in a box in that state; built on Object of Increased Size with a magnitude more (Base 4, +1 Conc, +1 size, +1 complexity; +5 maintains, +3 6/day). Panorama of the Heinzelmannchen (ReAn 10, Pen 0, 1/day, Touch, Momentary, Group): weaves wool into a described tapestry up to one hundred square paces, very quickly, Finesse Ease Factor 12 for a simple scene and more for complex ones (Base 1, +1 Touch, +2 Group, +1 size, +1 intricacy).

Magical cloth: she makes these charged items by Craft Magic, using her Casting Total, in days rather than a season, one sheet a day with usually one charge a sheet, and one effect only to a piece. She triggers them once the cloth is a garment, and Enduring Magic often lengthens them. For example, a Casting Total of 23 gives four sheets of the first below in four days. Iridescence of the Mallard's Head (MuIm 4, Personal, Month, Individual): dull green cloth turns iridescent, then reverts (Base 1, +3 Month). Staunch the Bloody Wound (CrCo 10, Touch, Month, Individual): bandages give +3 to Wound Recovery (Base 2, +1 Touch, +3 Month). Scintillation of the Phoenix (CrIg 10, Personal, Month, Individual): orange-yellow cloth glows and flickers like torchlight, liked by Flambeau for Tribunal robes (Base 3, +3 Month). Constrain the Shrewish Wife (MuMe 15, Touch, Moon, Individual): the wearer grows considerate of loved ones (Base 3, +1 Touch, +3 Moon). Curb the Straying Husband (MuMe 15, Touch, Moon, Individual): the wearer grows temperate, shunning drink, violence and philandering (Base 3, +1 Touch, +3 Moon). Cloth of Unicorn Hair (level 20, Touch, Sun, Individual): immunity to poison, a work of Craft Magic and so rolled as Dexterity + Craft, not cast; made rarely, and not truly of unicorn hair whatever she tells clients (Base 5, +1 Touch, +2 Sun). All are Pen 0.

Madder, Woad, and Weld: Touch, Month, Group. Dyes up to ten skeins of wool or five bolts of wool, cotton or linen any single hue chosen at casting; the cloth goes back to undyed when the spell ends. (Base 1, +1 Touch, +3 Month, +2 Group, +1 requisite)
The Unraveled Seam: Touch, Momentary, Part. Rots a thread of animal or plant origin so that the cloth it holds parts; it can be sewn again, so the garment counts as damaged, not destroyed. (Base 2, +1 Touch, +1 Part, +1 requisite)
The Wizard's Spindle: Touch, Momentary, Group. Cleans, cards and spins up to ten fleeces in a round; Finesse Ease Factor 12, or the wool is a useless tangle. (Base 1, +1 Touch, +2 Group)
Dressing the Human Form in Wool: Touch, Momentary, Individual; the spell lists printed level 15, which the errata corrects to 5. Makes one woollen garment from fleece (Finesse Ease Factor 12) or spun wool (9); finer work raises it, failure leaves a mess, and a new colour needs dye. Her usual way of tailoring her magical cloth. Uses the level 3 Rego Animal guideline from Covenants page 50. (Base 2, +1 Touch, +1 complexity)
Ward Against Faeries Which Creep and Crawl: Touch, Ring, Circle. Keeps out faerie animals of Might up to the spell's level. She casts it nightly with Circle of Beast Warding, sweeping the ground first so no spider is shut in with her.
Sealing the Lips: Voice, Sun, Individual; the new-spells section makes it ReCo, the spell lists MuCo. The target cannot speak, and looks to have his lips stitched, though that is only for show. (Base 2, +2 Voice, +2 Sun)
Clothe the Naked Form: Touch, Sun, Individual. Creates one garment of linen or cotton, mostly underclothes; Finesse Ease Factor 6 for standard quality, 9 to choose the dye's brightness and regional style. For when she has no cloth by her. (Base 1, +1 Touch, +2 Sun, +2 treated and processed)
The Clothier's Craft Done in an Instant: Touch, Momentary, Individual. Forms linen or cotton cloth into a garment; Finesse Ease Factor 9 for standard quality, as a day's work done at once, or the cloth is scraps. Working from raw fibre would need the level 5 guideline (Covenants page 51), which her Faerie Blood makes needless. (Base 3, +1 Touch)
The Mended Tear: Touch, Momentary, Part. A thread laid over a rent stitches it neatly; Finesse Ease Factor 6. (Base 3, +1 Touch, +1 Part)
Shearing the Unseen Sheep: Touch, Sun, Individual. Creates a fleece, the raw stuff she then turns into clothing by Rego craft magic. (Base 5, +1 Touch, +2 Sun)
The Unraveled Clothes: Voice, Momentary, Group. All stitches of thread or leather come undone and the victim is left naked; leather armour falls apart, and metal armour loses its padding, giving -3 to physical actions and half Protection until replaced. The clothes can be repaired. (Base 2, +2 Voice, +2 Group, +1 requisite)
Weaver's Trap of Threads: Voice, Sun, Group. A net of thick thread fills 5 paces by 5 by 6 feet, or hangs as a wall from supports; Strength stress roll Ease Factor 9 to get free, or an outsider with a blade takes three rounds. Fire is very effective but burns those caught; the net is not sticky. Her loathing of spiders made this a weaker answer to Weaver's Trap of Webs. (Base 2, +2 Voice, +2 Sun, +2 Group)
The Animate Attire: Voice, Concentration, Individual. One garment writhes at the caster's direction: -3 to all actions and 3 extra botch dice. Best on linen underclothes. (Base 5, +2 Voice, +1 Conc)

characters.summary:
A weaver of the Rusticani tradition (Houses of Hermes: Societates pages 130-133), who joins mundane craft to magic. She was born at Florum in the Normandy Tribunal (The Lion and the Lily page 96), of the de Spinnen family, whose blood comes from a faerie spider. Meeting that ancestor as a child left her terrified of him and of all spiders, so she would not train at Florum and was apprenticed to an associate of the covenant who taught her magical weaving.

A loner with no covenant, she sells her magical cloth to the rich: colours and effects no dye can give. She sells mostly through a middleman who cheats her badly, which she accepts because it keeps Quaesitores from looking at her. As the cloth's charges fade the customers return. Barred from society by her Gift, she follows it keenly through her vendor's gossip, and sometimes weaves impulses into fabric meant to better its wearer's life.

The spider prince resents being rejected and regularly sends his many-legged servants to torment her.

characters.name: Lambert of Merinita

invented_spells.name: Confusion of the Numbed Will
invented_spells.description: From the stat block in Magi of Hermes.

description.biography:
Tall, thin and dark-haired, greying at the temples, with a solemn look that makes him seem sadder than he acts, he usually dresses as a successful merchant. His easy smile is plainly practised, but its warmth goes a good way to offset The Gift.

Casting sigil: coins, worked subtly into what he makes, and clinking in the footsteps of creatures he enchants. Voting sigil: a wooden dowel carved as a caduceus, which he likes to turn into talk of Mercury's tie to trade.

Combat: fist Init -1, Attack -1, Defense -1, Damage 0; dodge Init -1, Defense -1. Soak +1. Encumbrance 0.

Vis: 4 pawns of Herbam in a wooden ring; 5 of Intellego in bottles of water from a reflecting pool, which keeps the moon's reflection wherever it goes.

Last 15 years: he runs the family business and spends much time with his grandchildren. At 47 he got a longevity ritual from a fellow magus in a deal costing two seasons, one assisting and one paying with his influence and wealth. One season upgraded his laboratory with the Highly Organized Virtue and an orb as a lesser feature (Covenants chapter 9). One season each inventing Memory of the Distant Dream, Confusion of the Numbed Will and Loss of But a Moment's Memory; two each on Familial Secrets (with help in the lab, by the errata), Oath Breaker's Confession and Opinions of the Masses; one each learning Mind Cleansed of Treachery and Thoughts Within Babble from Lab Texts; three on the Doorframe; three wholly with family. 110 xp in Abilities and 190 in Arts, with 25 more in Mentem from his Affinity. He has 2 xp past his Corpus score and 13 past Mentem.

Arcadian Travel: initiated through the Wayfarers by the script on page 80 of Houses of Hermes: Mystery Cults. His Ordeal took him from Bayeux cathedral to a faerie regio in the forested hills of Bayeux County, pursued by faerie boars; it gave him the Virtue and Fear (swine), and the cathedral is a permanent Arcane Connection to him. He makes charms with Profession: Storyteller, writing sections of his stories on paper as the charm's objects.

Casting tablet of Locked Storehouse (Covenants page 89), a spell he does not know: MuHe(Te) 45, Touch, Year +1, Structure, Ritual, Faerie. It turns a building and contents into a buried rock of hard igneous stone of about the same mass, for a year and a day; animal stuffs need an Animal requisite or the spell fails. The contents age but do not otherwise decay. The tablet calls for three pawns of Muto vis and six of Terram. (Base 4, +1 Touch, +4 Year+1, +3 Structure, +1 complexity)

Coins of Loose-Tongued Patrons: two silver coins with a crown on one side and Mercere on the other, each a lesser enchanted device of three pawns, got by trade and often held by his family, who value the honest feedback (though much use could Warp them). Blessing of Enthusiastic Patrons, on the Coin of Enthusiastic Patrons (Mercere laughing), and Curse of Petulant Customers, on the Coin of Petulant Customers (Mercere grimacing): ReMe 25, Pen 0, 1/day, Touch, Sun, Room; touched to a wall, they make those inside dwell on merchandise's good points (-6 to purchasers' Bargain rolls) or its faults (+6) (Base 10, +1 Touch, +2 Room).

Doorframe of the Wary Steward: he made this invested device to pay for the Coins and never keeps one, but has its Lab Texts to sell. Maple and hazel, built into a covenant, with a small bell on a nail in a hollow at the top; opened with eight pawns, four in use. Its power (InMe 35, Pen 0, Special, Momentary, Individual) shakes the frame and rings the bell if a creature passing believes it means the residents harm; animals are unaffected, and the Limit of the Infernal applies (Base 15, +1 Touch equivalent, +1 non-standard range, +10 unlimited).

Soothing Voice of the Stableman: Voice, Sun, Individual. Plants in an animal's mind that the caster is a safe friend. It cannot lift the unease of The Gift, but a beast cannot tie that unease to the caster; mounts stay skittish, with Ease Factors 3 higher and extra botch dice where mood matters, and the Blatant Gift sends them into a frenzy. Animals Warped by it turn belligerent and frightened. (Base 2, +2 Voice, +2 Sun, +1 size)
Patch of Drought: Voice, Momentary, Individual. Destroys the water in a puddle or patch of mud up to 20 paces across, speeding carts on wet roads. (Base 4, +2 Voice)
Tread of Fellow Travelers: Road, Diameter, Group, Faerie. Gives the number, consciousness, direction and distance of the nearest group of minds on his road, one way. Merinitae use such spells to sense targets for other Road-range magic, which the law of Arcane Connections otherwise bars. (Base 5, +2 Road, +1 Diameter, +2 Group)
Blissful Messenger: Touch, Until, Individual, Faerie, Ritual. Replaces memory of an event with memory of another; it ends when the target speaks of it to a chosen person, who must figure in the altered memory. A Tytalus maga arranged for him to learn it as an apprentice to serve her agents. Vis and distrust of the Gifted keep it rare. (Base 5, +1 Touch, +4 Until)
Calm Mind of Resolute Behavior: Personal, Diameter, Individual. Banishes all emotion: appeals to feeling fail and no Personality Trait rolls can be made, though goals and memories stay. His mater thought it vital for dealing with faeries; he uses it to weigh large choices, dislikes it, and fears botching Perdo Mentem on himself. (Base 15, +1 Diameter)
Pull of Blood: Touch, Momentary, Bloodline, Faerie. Gives the direction and distance of each living descendant of the target; he uses it on himself to keep track of his family. (Base 4, +1 Touch, +3 Bloodline)
Scent of Loose Purses: Touch, Sun, Smell. The target smells desire and interest in minds nearby, stronger as they are stronger. Lambert uses it to train his family and staff to read people, pairing them to learn the cues without magic. (Base 5, +1 Touch, +2 Sun, +2 Smell)
Stench of Hate: Touch, Sun, Smell. As Scent of Loose Purses, for antipathy, dislike and hate. (Base 5, +1 Touch, +2 Sun, +2 Smell)
Familial Secrets: Touch, Momentary, Bloodline, Faerie (level and Range by the errata). He learns what each descendant believes the answer to a question to be, as Posing the Silent Question, with no Arcane Connection. To tell whose answer is whose, Perception + Awareness Ease Factor 3 + number of descendants, more if some are unfamiliar. Made not to Warp his bloodline. (Base 15, +1 Touch, +3 Bloodline)
Opinions of the Masses: Personal, Concentration, Hearing. Each mind met answers a chosen question in a voice he hears, clear if it has dwelt on the matter, whispering if not, silent if it never has or resists; he has heard spirits and unseen creatures so. Crowds raise Ease Factors for listening. (Base 15, +1 Conc, +3 Hearing)
Oath Breaker's Confession: Eye, Bargain and Momentary, Individual, Faerie. The new-spells section gives level 35, the spell lists 40. Cast on striking a bargain; if the target breaks it within a year he knows at once, and why and how she thinks she broke it. (Base 15, +1 Eye, +3 Momentary and Bargain)
Mind Cleansed of Treachery: Eye, Bargain and Momentary, Individual, Faerie. Cast on striking a bargain; if the target breaks it within a year his memory is destroyed, losing all ideas, identity, and every Academic, Arcane, Martial and Supernatural Ability and Art. General Abilities stay, as do remembered faces and places, without meaning. Traded from a Merinita for the Lab Text of Oath Breaker's Confession. (Base 25, +1 Eye, +3 Momentary and Bargain)

characters.summary:
Born to a merchant family, Lambert loved haggling from childhood, but his Gift undid his charm and enthusiasm. He stayed close to his family all through his apprenticeship, marrying and fathering children before it ended, and providing for them has shaped his life. The family buys goods and carries them to where they sell at a profit; his magic finds the best buys and moves them safely and fast. His magic centres on Mentem, Faerie Magic and the family's trade.

He must haggle whenever he can, with mixed results. Mortals and faeries who deal with him often suspect they were cheated without knowing why, but magi are shielded from his Gift, so striking deals with the Order delights him.

As he ages he hands the face-to-face trade to his children, for fear of the charge of interfering with mundanes, and takes his bargaining to the fay in faerie auras and regiones, which earns him the enmity of a powerful group of faerie merchants. By his last printing he lives among children, grandchildren and great-grandchildren, his passion given to studying faeries.

characters.name: Maris of Tytalus

invented_spells.name: Comfort the Drenched Caster
invented_spells.description: From the stat block in Magi of Hermes.

description.biography:
Life at sea keeps him far stronger than most magi.

Twilight scar: his hair is slightly animate and wriggles by itself.

Casting sigil: he seizes unseen threads between himself and the target and weaves them into the effect. Voting token: a snowflake bound in a spiral.

Combat: dodge Init +1, Defense +3; fist Init +1, Attack +2, Defense +2, Damage +1; kick Init 0, Attack +2, Defense +1, Damage +4; harpoon Init +3, Attack +5, Defense +3, Damage +8. Soak +2. Encumbrance 0.

Last 15 years: a decade at sea perfecting his hunt for treasures the deep has claimed, until a storm drew him and the ship into a huge vortex and helpful merfolk saved them. Back on Slvolder he went on working to beat Natura's every challenge. Ten years of experience at sea, five on the island.

Slvolder and Ormurin Langi: the ballad tells of King Olaf Tryggvason, who forced Christianity on Norway, and whose flagship the Long Serpent was doomed by Eirikr Hakonarson in the third attack of a great battle, said to be in the Oresund Straight near the lost isle of Slvolder; he and his crew leapt overboard. Maris found it in a storm his magic could not touch. It lies in a misty magical regio that opens only for one truly in peril of being lost at sea, and no other way in is known. He keeps a permanent lab there. So he returns only when failing against Natura; each return teaches him a lesson and gives the means to answer it. The day he can no longer reach it, he will hold his vow fulfilled.

Voices in the Ocean: unaided, no words and only subtle gestures can be used to cast underwater, at the normal penalties. Voice-range spells cast submerged reach only targets in or touching the surface of the water. After each 10 meters of descent, a character loses a tenth of his depth minus Soak (armour not counted) in Fatigue Levels: at 50 meters with Soak 3, two levels, and three more on going ten deeper.

Talisman, the Paregro Mare: a ship of his own building, mixing Knarr and Buss, with a longship's oars she is not built to use, a lower deck in place of a shallow draft, single-masted, with about 30 tons of cargo, up to 10 knots at best, and a cramped sanctum below. He has nearly lived aboard since leaving the Novgorod Tribunal. Attunements: +4 affect currents, +4 affect dead wood, +4 Aquam, +4 banish weather, +4 create or control winds, +7 protection from storms.

Its effects, all Pen 0. Save Our Ship (PeAq 27, 3/day, Touch, Momentary, Room): all water in the hold is destroyed, liquids stored there too, and everything left slightly dry (Base 10, +1 Touch, +2 Room; +2 3/day). Eye of the Storm (ReAq 8, constant, Personal, Sun, Individual): waves part round her, so rough seas add nothing to sailing Ease Factors, though strong winds do, and she is very hard to swamp (Base 2, +2 Sun; +1 2/day, +3 sun). Ward the Drowning Waves (ReAq 33, 6/day, Touch, Conc, Room): clears water from the lower hold and keeps it out long enough for repairs (Base 5, +1 Touch, +1 Conc, +2 Room; +3 6/day, +5 maintains). Control the Reckless Vessel (ReAq(Au) 35, 24/day, Touch, Conc, Individual): wind and currents drive her, holding heading and speed while he is elsewhere, sailing without him on deck, and holding station with the rudder raised, even where too deep to anchor; +7 to sailing checks (Base 4, +1 Touch, +1 Conc, +2 Size, +1 requisite; +5 24/day, +5 maintains). Hull of Unbreakable Iron (MuHe(Te) 24, constant, Personal, Sun, Individual): metal-hard hull, immune to ramming; a captain who rams wrecks himself if he fails the contested Int + Profession by more than his Profession (Base 4, +2 Sun, +2 Size; +1 2/day, +3 sun). Helios' Companionship (CrIg 29, constant, Touch, Sun, Group, by the errata): torchlight and summer warmth below, which by Covenants pages 118-119 gives the lab Magical Lighting and Magical Heating (Superior) as free Virtues (printed Base 3, +2 Sun, +2 Room, +1 heat; +1 2/day, +3 sun, before the errata's changes).

Items he has designed; the book does not date them. All are Pen 0; below, 2/day, sun stands for +1 2/day and +3 for a trigger at sunrise and sunset. Ever-Tempting Trap, tailored to a prey, his for cod: +5 to fishing. Sight of Wounded Prey (CrIm 14, constant, Touch, Sun, Individual): an illusion of bait, seen and smelled (Base 3, +1 Touch, +2 Sun; 2/day, sun).

Eyeglass of Nereus, a rusty eyepiece. True Sight of the Air (InAu 25, 24/day, Touch, Conc, Vision; Base 1, +1 Touch, +1 Conc, +4 Vision; +5 24/day, +5 maintains). Eyes of the Eagle (InIm 35, 24/day, Touch, Conc, Vision; Base 3, +1 Touch, +1 Conc, +4 Vision; +5 24/day, +5 maintains).

Foul Weather's Bane, a cloak: +5 Soak against exposure, and neither freezes nor gathers ice. Cloak of the Duck's Feathers (ReAq 9, constant, Touch, Sun, Individual; Base 2, +2 Sun, +1 Touch; 2/day, sun). Comfort the Weary Traveler (CrIg 9, constant, Touch, Sun, Individual): warmth against the worst winter (same build).

Gorget of Salty Breath, for working normally underwater. Lungs of the Fish (MuAq(Au) 24, constant, Touch, Sun, Part; Base 4, +1 Touch, +2 Sun, +1 Part; 2/day, sun), which gives too little air to speak spells. Surviving the Deep (MuCo 30, 1/day, Touch, Sun, Individual): body resists the deep, +3 Soak (Base 15, +1 Touch, +2 Sun). The Kraken's Song (MuIm 8, constant, Touch, Sun, Individual): voice becomes a loud high click that carries Voice-range spells through water (Base 1, +1 Touch, +2 Sun; 2/day, sun).

The Nailed Down Chamber Pot, nailed to the deck. Remove the Unsightly Mess (PeCo(Aq) 20, unlimited, Touch, Momentary, Individual; Base 4, +1 Touch, +1 requisite; +10 unlimited).

Neptune's Anchors, small weights on a long rope trailed behind the ship, which draws taut toward magical sites; Intelligence + Navigation Ease Factor 9 fixes a site well enough to dive. Guide the Seeker (ReHe 16, constant, Personal, Momentary, Individual; Base 3; +3 linked, +10 unlimited). Seek the Enchanted Waters (InVi 19, constant, Vision, Sun, Individual): finds nearby vis (Base 1, +4 Vision, +2 Sun; 2/day, sun).

Naiad's Cask. Cleanse Gaia's Tears (PeTe(Aq) 20, 24/day, Touch, Momentary, Individual): destroys all salt, leaving other impurities (Base 3, +1 Touch, +2 Mineral, +1 complex; +5 24/day).

Roll of Endless Rope, a vine on a spindle that gives ten feet a tug; it may be cut off as long as five feet stay coiled. Rigging of it needs replacing each duration. Concoct Cordage (CrHe 15, unlimited, Touch, Moon, Individual; Base 1, +1 Touch, +3 Moon; +10 unlimited).

Shroud of the Healed Body, bearing the cross of St. John. Hospitaller's Vigil (CrCo 24, constant, Touch, Sun, Individual): worn for a wound or sickness's duration, +12 to recovery (Base 5, +1 Touch, +2 Sun; 2/day, sun).

Tryggvason's Chart, a circle of cured leather on the navigation console with a weighted line trailed astern, showing the sea around in real time: +5 Navigation for one who knows its notation. Reveal the Ocean's Secrets (InAq 19, constant, Touch, Sun, Part): motion, speed and bounds of the ocean up to 1500 feet all round (Base 3, +1 Touch, +2 Sun, +1 Part, +2 Size, +1 complexity; 2/day, sun). Visualize the Water's Flow (CrIm 11, constant, Touch, Sun, Individual): draws that as a map in his own notation (Base 1, +1 Touch, +2 Sun; 2/day, sun, +3 linked).

Repel Winter's Clutches: Touch, Concentration, Individual. Warms the target from within, to defrost a thing or save a freezing person; +5 to Medicine rolls for hypothermia. (Base 3, +1 Touch, +1 Conc)

characters.summary:
A Calliclean Tytalus who thought the Order's covenants and their help, meant or not, spoiled the great conflict. Wanting a rival tougher and less fickle than Nomos, he left it for Natura, vowing to take no aid from anyone until he has mastered her. He lives alone on the Baltic in his ship, the Paregro Mare, with no friend or teacher. Ashore on his island sanctuary of Slvolder in the Oresund Straight he works in his lab, finding ways to ease life at sea and meet what Natura sends; at sea he gathers supplies, tends underwater gardens, and trawls for ancient magical sites lost beneath the waves where others cannot or will not go.

One storm, seemingly with a life of its own, wrecks each of his plans: it strands him on Slvolder, nearly drowns him in a vortex until helpful merfolk save him, and later capsizes the Paregro Mare. In his last printing he sets out on the first day of the new year 1300 swearing never to return, and the Order loses him.

characters.name: Marcus Tauros

invented_spells.name: Growth of Creeping Things
invented_spells.description: From the stat block in Magi of Hermes.

invented_spells.name: Soothe the Ferocious Boar
invented_spells.description: From the stat block in Magi of Hermes.

invented_spells.name: Blunt the Viper's Fangs
invented_spells.description: From the stat block in Magi of Hermes.

description.biography:
Massive: eight feet tall and broad with it, in simple clothes, shoulders hunched in a vain try at hiding his size. Olive skin, black hair, and a beard trimmed close to the jaw, with no moustache. The stigmata of the Path of Seeming show as an interlocking labyrinth round his forehead, which shifts as he does magic, as if tracing his way through the maze.

Casting sigil: horns, usually in shadow or as a ghostly image. Voting sigil: a bronze bull's head.

Warped Magic: his organs glow through his skin as he casts, by the spell's Form: Animal and Auram the liver; Aquam and Imaginem the brain; Corpus and Vim the heart; Herbam and Terram the spleen; Ignem and Mentem the gallbladder.

Twilight scars: his shadow has horns; the third and fourth fingers of each hand have fused; he leaves cloven footprints; his Gift draws flies, not repels them.

Combat: dodge Init -1, Defense +1. Soak +7 with the Mark of Protection on his belly exposed. Encumbrance 0. Equipment: peasant clothing, Canopic Jars, Mark of Protection.

Last 15 years: initiated into the third Station of the Path of Seeming (a season); two seasons on four Canopic Jars; three enchanting the abdomen tattoo; one on the second lab effect; two investigating the Minoan labyrinth at Knossos, with insight into its ancient magic; two stabilizing his research, now 25 breakthrough points in all. 135 levels of spells invented or learned, 105 xp in Abilities and 140 in Arts.

Original Research (Houses of Hermes: True Lineages pages 26-30): he seeks a Major Breakthrough into a Hermetic Virtue, Hermetic Metamorphosis, believing the Counter-Cyclical Alam (Houses of Hermes: Mystery Cults page 47), the mirror of our world across the Wheel of Time, moves from chaos toward harmony: first lone organs, then creatures, then chimeras, and at last all life combined. He holds the chimeric beasts of antiquity to be more harmonious than those of today and wants to remake them, which Hermetic magic forbids. The Wizard's Mount, Prying Eyes and The Beast Remade he also invented, gaining 5 points from the last.

The Labyrinth of the Open Mind: his laboratory floor, of pale and dark-stained wood in a labyrinth, furniture and tools set at mystic points, each path a different effect (Covenants page 121). Opened with 10 pawns of Vim vis, three effects using 9. All Pen 0. Path to Serendipitous Discovery (CrVi 24, constant, Touch, Sun, Room): taints the sanctum, +2 lab specialization in Experimentation but Warping Score +1 (Base 3, +1 Touch, +2 Sun, +2 Room; +1 2/day, +3 environmental). Path to Enlightened Operations (ReAn 20, unlimited, Touch, Conc, Room): items of animal stuff float where released, drifting into propitious order, General Quality +1 (Base 1, +1 Touch, +1 Conc, +2 Room; +10 unlimited, +5 maintains). Path of Shadows Beneath the Skin (InCo(An) 40, 1/day, Touch, Conc, Vision): a magical sense of internal organs, +2 lab specialization in Corpus and in Animal (Base 5, +1 Conc, +4 Vision, +1 requisite; +5 maintains).

Canopic Jars: four alabaster figures 18 inches tall with hawk, lion, baboon and human heads as lids, after the Egyptian jars; lesser enchantments, made two to a season, to keep the hearts of his subjects. Halt Corruption's Work (CrCo 9, Pen 0, constant, Touch, Sun, Individual): an organ inside does not rot (Base 2, +1 Touch, +2 Sun; +1 2/day, +3 environmental).

The Mark of Protection: a tattoo of the sun in glory over his whole abdomen, invested with 6 pawns (material 2, multiplier 3 for size; Houses of Hermes: Mystery Cults page 51). Its purple murex ink and crushed shells give +2 Shape and Material for protection. Resilience of Theseus (MuCo 39, Pen 0, constant, Touch, Sun, Individual): +4 Soak, but by an experimental flaw only while the tattoo is uncovered (Base 20, +1 Touch, +2 Sun; +1 2/day, +3 environmental).

Worm of the Soil: Touch, Sun, Individual. Creates a beetle; every invertebrate counts as a worm in Mythic Europe. No breakthrough. (Base 5, +1 Touch, +2 Sun)
Flight Perfected: Touch, Sun, Individual. Creates a dove in the hands, a normal bird for the duration. No breakthrough. (Base 10, +1 Touch, +2 Sun)
Flight Divorced: Touch, Sun, Part. Creates a joined pair of living bird wings, flapping at random, having no mind or senses; loose indoors they give -3 to rolls needing concentration and an extra botch die. Gave a breakthrough in the first of two seasons. (Base 10, +1 Touch, +2 Sun, +1 Part)
Bushy Tail of the Branch-Dancer: Touch, Sun, Individual. A squirrel's tail: +3 to keep balance. (Base 2, +1 Touch, +2 Sun, requisite free)
Sure-Footedness of the Crag-Leaper: Touch, Sun, Individual. A mountain goat's hooves: +3 on steep climbs and descents. (Base 2, +1 Touch, +2 Sun, requisite free)
Webbed Toes of the Pond-Dweller: Touch, Sun, Individual. A frog's feet: +3 to swim in still or slow water. (Base 2, +1 Touch, +2 Sun, requisite free)
Kiss of the Enigma: Touch, Momentary, Individual. The target takes two Warping Points, and a magus checks for Twilight. Meant to bring out monstrous traits in caged animals, with random results. Invented three times before a breakthrough; the two earlier versions had Side Effects, changing hair colour and making skin transparent. (Base 10, +1 Touch)
Strength Extinguished: Touch, Sun, Part. Creates a bull's heart. No breakthrough. (Base 10, +1 Touch, +2 Sun, +1 Part)
Strength Renewed: Touch, Sun, Part. Creates a bull's heart that beats strongly. Three seasons gave a breakthrough, and experimentation left a flaw: it beats only in light, faintly in shadow and like a drum in full sun. (Base 15, +1 Touch, +2 Sun, +1 Part)
Slime of the Muck-Dweller: Touch, Sun, Individual. An eel's slimy skin: +6 Defense against grappling. (Base 2, +1 Touch, +2 Sun, requisite free)
Spirit of the Bull of Minos: Touch, Year, Individual, Ritual. The target's heart is swapped for a bull's, harmlessly if cast rightly, granting Reserves of Strength. At the year's end he can restore a well-kept heart; otherwise the target dies. From an Insight (Ancient Magic pages 8-9) after he read a sacrificial knife's memories under Knossos, left by the Minoan Cult of the Bull. (Base 2, +1 Touch, +4 Year; level 20 as a ritual)

characters.summary:
A giant-blooded Criamon who wants to make living beings by combining existing creatures, the minotaur above all. His size shames him: cruelly teased as a child, he was deeply grateful to the master who took him from those who feared his Gift and showed him how to better himself, and he still grows angry when anyone mentions his height, however kindly. That master, an anatomist, taught him the body and fostered his gift with its organs.

Initiated into House Criamon's mysteries, he saw a past life as a Minoan priest on Crete who made the minotaur from a man and a sacred bull. If he can repeat that across the Wheel of Time, he believes, he can mend what he hates in his body and mind; finishing the work would likely lift his Low Self-Esteem and give him a Confidence Score of 1. The obsession has cost him the usual marks of Hermetic maturity: no familiar, no apprentice, and no talisman until forty years a magus.

He digs at the ruined palace of Knossos, whose catacombs held objects of the Minoan Cult of the Bull, and by his last printing stands on the edge of his breakthrough.

description.biography:
A beautiful mature woman with a beguiling smile. She keeps her long russet hair in a crespine, a net fixed to the back of her coif, and dresses simply, in a woollen dress and kirtle with a leather bodice.

Casting sigil: doubling; targets sometimes bear a ghostly after-effect, shadow or echo. Voting sigil: a silver bracelet set with an onyx.

Twilight scars: her eyes shine faintly green in the dark; her clothes darken through the day and lighten by night; all ale within 3 paces turns to water.

Combat: dodge Init 0, Defense 0. Soak +1. Encumbrance 0. Equipment: Coins of Mirth (0 to 13), Bracelet of Clandestine Insignificance, Pigeon Amulets (0 to 2).

Her Warping Score is printed 3 (45), and points past 3 cannot pass 19, so the sheet holds 3 (15): the book's 45 reads as her total.

Last 15 years: three seasons on three more Signet effects; two Pigeon Amulets; she began an apprentice, four seasons so far. 71 xp in Abilities, 95 levels of spells, 224 xp in Arts; Secondary Insight adds 32 in Forms and 26 in Techniques. She has 5 xp past her Muto score and 5 past Imaginem.

Coin of Mirth: charged items in the form of a low coin of the realm, passed to unknowing dupes for street food or trinkets and set off together with Trigger the Distant Power; two or three people bursting out laughing cover her vulgar magic. Touch of Hilarity (CrMe 10, Pen 0, charged, Touch, Diameter, Individual), usually triggered by a chuckling sound (Base 4, +1 Touch, +1 Diam).

Bracelet of Clandestine Insignificance: a simple silver bangle, a lesser enchantment of two pawns. Hiding in Plain Sight (MuIm 14, Pen 0, 24/day, Touch, Conc, Individual): species shed turn anamorphic, so while the wearer acts harmlessly and draws no notice, attention glides off her; speaking to someone ends it for them. The viewer rolls Perception -3 (two senses) against a die + his Inattentive or similar Trait + the wielder's Perception + her Finesse, and must beat it by 3 to see through it (Houses of Hermes: Societates pages 65-66). She avoids wearing it near magi, who could charge her with scrying (Base 2, +1 Touch, +1 Conc; +5 maintains, +5 24/day).

Signet of Hallam: a gold ring with an onyx seal, opened with 12 pawns, 11 of effects in the end. It disguises the wearer as Lord Richard of Hallam, once a close friend of her covenant, whose sudden death would have lost it an ally; after covering his absence she made the ring so anyone could play him. Rubbed with the words vir Hallamus or mulier Hallamae (the second for women, adding the last change), each effect starts in turn, one a round. All Touch, Pen 0, and cancellable at will.

Face of Lord Richard (MuCo 16, 2/day, Conc, Part): black hair, green eyes, clean shaven, like Disguise of the New Visage (Base 3, +1 Touch, +1 Conc, +1 Part; +1 2/day, +5 maintains). Voice of Lord Richard (MuIm 9, 2/day, Conc, Individual): deep, with a distinct Norman accent, like Voice of the Leucrota (Base 1, +1 Touch, +1 Conc; +1 2/day, +5 maintains). Clothes of Lord Richard (MuAn(He) 16, 2/day, Conc, Group): black wool doublet and hose worked with red, white linen shirt, riding boots and cape, felt hat with a red feather, gloves, like Remake the Tailor's Craft (Base 2, +1 Touch, +1 Conc, +2 Group; +1 2/day, +5 maintains). Body of the Virile Male (MuCo 11, 2/day, Conc, Individual): male form only, with mulier Hallamae (Base 3, +1 Touch, +1 Conc; +1 2/day, +5 maintains). Masking the Odor of Magic (PeVi 34, constant, Sun, Group): hides the ring's effects from Intellego Vim up to level 30 and Magic Sensitivity below 6, added after a churchman with that Ability made trouble (Base effect 5, +1 Touch, +2 Sun, +2 Group; +1 2/day, +3 environmental).

Pigeon Amulet: a brass coin stamped with a bird and holed for a thong, made as a pair from one batch; she keeps one half, neatly labelled on her wall, as an Arcane Connection to the other for years, and gives the charged half to possible agents or skilled operatives. Take Me Home (ReMe 25, Pen 0, charged, Touch, Moon, Individual): a nagging urge to go to a place set at making, which in about a week usually moves them; typically triggered by a bee's buzz through Trigger the Distant Power (Base 5, +1 Touch, +3 Moon).

Companion: Kore (Marie-Philipe), her elder sister, an inch taller and as russet-haired, burned down the left of her body so that her face sets in a sneer. Her hands shake, so she crosses them tightly on her chest, and she goes in a hooded dark wool cloak. Int +3, Per 0, Pre +3, Com -3, Str +1, Sta +1, Dex -1, Qik 0. Size 0. Confidence 1 (3). Virtues and Flaws: Wise One; Entrancement, Hex (Realms of Power: The Infernal page 85); Arcane Lore, Strong Willed, True Love (sister); Enemy, Hatred; Disfigured, Offensive to Animals, Palsied Hands, Reclusive. Traits: Wrathful +3, Ruthless +3, Devoted to Sister +2, Secretive +1. Knife Init 0, Attack +4, Defense +4, Damage +3. Soak +1.

Kore +30: age 54 (51), Pre +3 (2), Str +1 (1), Dex -1 (1), Decrepitude 0 (4), Warping 2 (6), Compulsion (hand washing) from Warping. Area Lore 1 (around covenant), Artes Liberales 2 (grammar), Awareness 2 (people hiding), Brawl 4 (knife), Chirurgy 3 (on sister), Church Lore 1 (corrupt priests), Entrancement 5 (5) (men), Folk Ken 3 (magi), French 5 (Norman), Guile 4 (to magi), Hex 7 (sudden fires), Infernal Lore 4 (curses), Intrigue 3 (magi), Latin 4 (Hermetic), Leadership 4 (agents), Magic Lore 4 (fire spirits), Magic Theory 3 (spells), Order of Hermes Lore 3 (local tribunal), Penetration 4 (Hex), Profession: Apothecary 4 (poisons), Stealth 3 (avoiding attention).

Voice of the Leucrota: Touch, Sun, Individual. Changes the voice wholly, to a known person's, an accent heard, or just a different one, without granting languages; Intelligence + Finesse Ease Factor 6 for an accent, 9 for a voice. She uses it to humiliate those she beats at certamen. (Base 1, +1 Touch, +2 Sun)
Aura of Childlike Innocence: Touch, Sun, Individual. As Aura of Ennobled Presence, for seeming guileless: +3 to deflect suspicion or convince of innocence, though to those feeling the Gift it reads as sanctimony (first printed in Houses of Hermes: Societates page 96). (Base 3, +1 Touch, +2 Sun)
My Old and Dear Friend: Eye, Sun, Individual. The target recalls her doing him a major recent favour, in a guise she picks, and cannot be talked out of it until the spell ends, when he sees the deception. (Base 4, +1 Eye, +2 Sun, +1 complexity)
I Was Never Here: Eye, Momentary, Individual. The target forgets meeting her, if any contact was brief, trivial and within a day: an overt spell or a gate let pass, but not who stabbed him. (Base 4, +1 Eye)
Remake the Tailor's Craft: Touch, Sun, Group. Reshapes a set of mostly animal-stuff clothes, keeping substance and colour, though the number of garments may change; Intelligence + Finesse Ease Factor 6, 9 if very different. Plant parts need a Herbam requisite, purely plant clothes cannot be changed, and fastenings stay. (Base 2, +1 Touch, +2 Sun, +2 Group)
Trigger the Distant Power: Arcane Connection, Momentary, Individual. Sounds a chosen noise, never a voice or words, near what she has a connection to; she sets off charged items held by agents with a whine, buzz or chirrup that passes for an insect. (Base 1, +4 Arc)
The Factor's Roll Call: Eye, Momentary, Individual. Shows if the target ever heard a given word. Her factors say an obscure one, usually shibboleth, to recruits, so she can tell her agents and whether she has been exposed. (Base 15, +1 Eye)
Funding the Blackmailer's Purse: Eye, Momentary, Individual. Given some hint of its subject, reveals a deep secret in full; it cannot fish at random. If a grog flinches at a word, the spell can show the old theft behind it and where the loot lies. (Base 25, +1 Eye)

characters.summary:
Marie-Helene and her elder sister Marie-Philipe came from a village near a covenant. A Tytalus magus took the younger as apprentice and refused the other, who had only a latent knack and no Gift. Soon a terrible fire struck the family home and scarred Marie-Philipe; Marie-Helene, sure her master set it to rid her of a distraction, hid her sister, slipping out by night with food and lessons, though the elder could work no spell. At her Gauntlet she took the name Persephone of Tytalus, and her sister Kore. They swore a fiery end for him: plain revenge, nothing to do with the House's beloved rivals. Kore keeps to the shadows nearby, hiding her face.

Persephone runs a network of agents who mostly do not know whom they serve, reached through go-betweens or in disguise. They are chiefly spies, whose reports Kore sifts. Her spells and enchantments serve the network, and her plans have drifted from revenge to general meddling in her Tribunal's politics. Her covenant goes on impersonating the dead Lord Richard of Hallam with her ring, which it uses only to protect its interests; she is less careful when she wears the disguise. His widow Joanna knows and is glad, preferring it to the dull second husband her family would find her.

She rarely keeps an agent long for fear of double agents (Houses of Hermes: Societates pages 140-144). Typical ones, each with the Trait that binds them: Macco, a novice scribe at a rival covenant (Fear of Discovery +1); Sir Stephene, a wealthy knight and secret lycanthrope promised a cure (Hopeful of a Cure +3); Pierre, a journeyman with a guildmaster as mentor in a distant shoemakers' guild (Ambitious +1); Jack, a well-travelled peddler of penny cures full of local gossip (Avaricious +1); Claude, the sisters' cousin, a nobleman's trusted man-at-arms who can lend his men (Loyal to Sisters +3); Sister Maurisse, a mendicant nun who thinks the sisters need protection (Pity +2).
characters.secrets: Kore hates the pater more fiercely than Persephone does: Persephone's resentment is considered, Kore's visceral. Thinking her sister distracted by being a maga, she has taken up the vendetta herself. Without Persephone's knowledge, mundane agents, sometimes with stolen magical devices, watch him always; she has struck at him in secret with Hex, and holds one of his lesser enchantments, knowing it to be an Arcane Connection. She covers her tracks with great care, knowing the danger to her sister, who can truthfully tell Quaesitores she knows nothing.

invented_spells.description: From the stat block in Magi of Hermes.

description.biography:
Heavier now and bearing himself as an ageing man despite his ritual, in weighty robes edged with embossed leather and covered in mystical and mathematical signs. Twilight scar: his fingers are unnaturally long. He carries pawns of vis to display his wealth. The Sense the Weight spells and The Unseen Arm are Hermetic Numerology rotes.

Since the last block: initiated into the Cononites, whose trust he won quickly, turning from the Verditius Mysteries. His initiations have left him all but unable to use spontaneous magic, so he leans on casting tablets from his brother Cononites (Covenants p. 89); assume any reasonable Intellego spell up to fourth magnitude. He began to experiment with ligatures (Art & Academe p. 68).

Combat: dodge Init -1, Defense +0; fist Init -1, Attack +3, Defense +0, Damage -1; knife Init -1, Attack +5, Defense +1, Damage +1. Soak +0.

Cloth shears, an Item of Quality invested with The Perfect Fit: +2 to rolls to make or mend clothing, and the same to Finesse rolls for their Rego Craft Magic. The book describes no effect by that name.

Sanctum door hanging, a tapestry with a white sanctum marker on deep red, showing damnation and death up close, carried to protect a temporary sanctum. Come No Further (CrMe 45, Pen +12, constant, expires after 70 years): those approaching need a Brave stress roll of 9 to touch it. The Weight of All Perdition Be Upon You (Cr(Pe)Me(Co) 35, Pen +20, unlimited, expires after 70 years): touching it burns with painless agony and demonic voices; a Brave roll of 9 to pass, at -3 if already affected by Come No Further.

Loom, an Item of Quality: +4 to all mundane weaving, and invested with A Day's Worth of Weaving twice a day, the bonus aiding its Finesse.

Talisman: the Distaff of Petalichus, a four-sided black greatstaff with white symbols set out in mathematical ratios. Attunements: +4 control things at a distance, +4 destroy things at a distance. The Invisible Eye Revealed variant (InVi 29, Pen +0, constant) senses every scrying up to level 30, whether or not it breaches his Parma. The Gaze of Others (CrIg 17, Pen +0, 50/day), triggered by it, makes some inscriptions softly glow.

Spell notes: Arachne's Tuition is ReCo 25 with Touch Range by the errata, not the 20 and Eye the blocks and p. 101 print; he uses it to move an apprentice's limbs from within, adding 1 to a season's Source Quality for physical crafts, at 1 Warping point a year for each two seasons of it. A Day's Worth of Spinning and of Weaving are Rego Craft Magic, with Perception + Finesse against the craft's Ease Factor; a bolt is two paces by one, and Herbam requisites apply to plant cloth.

characters.summary: Petalichus the Weaver, last of Arachne's Children, a dwindling cult of Verditius weavers who put magic into humble cloth while others forged swords and rings. His learning in philosophy and the artes liberales drew the Cononites, a secret Hermetic cult guarding the esoteric works of Conon of Samos, Euclid, Apollonius and Archimedes; they taught him their magic and he made their tools. Modest in his crafts and lofty in his aims, he is secretive, manipulative and vindictive, working from hiding through agents and proxies, and a long feud with Solar Magnus of Tytalus runs through his life.
characters.secrets: Quaesitor Valeria of Donum Chanuti found evidence that he killed Thomas Roxbury, a notary of House Guernicus, with a Light of Fell Disease candle while hunting Solar Magnus at Canterbury. He destroyed Solar Magnus there with a Dreams You Shall Not Wake From sheet, having learned when the Tytalus's cyclic magic left his resistance weakest. He bought Let the Sun Not Bother Me This Day from Yestin of Jerbiton for use in that feud.

characters.name: Ranulf of Flambeau

params.circumstance: spells of Range Sight or Eye

invented_spells.name: Wizard's Boost Ignem
invented_spells.description: From the stat block in Magi of Hermes.

invented_spells.name: Gather Essence of the Beast
